title: 2 Chronicles 13
paragraphs: ¹ In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam, Abijah began to reign over Judah. ² He reigned three years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Michaiah daughter of Uriel of Gibeah. There was war between Abijah and Jeroboam. ³ Abijah took the field with an army of four hundred thousand fighting men, while Jeroboam drew up a battle line against him with eight hundred thousand chosen warriors. ⁴ Abijah stood on Mount Zemaraim in the hill country of Ephraim and called out, "Hear me, Jeroboam and all Israel! ⁵ Don't you know that the LORD, the God of Israel, gave the kingship over Israel to David and his descendants forever by a covenant of salt?"

⁶ "Yet Jeroboam son of Nebat, a servant of Solomon son of David, rose up and rebelled against his master. ⁷ Worthless scoundrels rallied around him and overpowered Rehoboam son of Solomon when he was young and indecisive and couldn't resist them. ⁸ And now you plan to resist the kingdom of the LORD, which is in the hands of David's descendants. You are indeed a vast army, and you have with you the golden calves that Jeroboam made as your gods. ⁹ But haven't you driven out the priests of the LORD, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites? Haven't you appointed your own priests as the peoples of other lands do? Anyone who comes to consecrate himself with a young bull and seven rams can become a priest of what are not gods. ¹⁰ As for us, the LORD is our God, and we have not abandoned him. The sons of Aaron are our priests who serve the LORD, and the Levites assist them.

¹¹ "Every morning and every evening they present burnt offerings and fragrant incense to the LORD. They set out the bread of the Presence on the ceremonially clean table, and they light the golden lampstand and its lamps each evening. We are keeping the requirements of the LORD our God. But you have abandoned him. ¹² God is with us — he is our leader. His priests are here with their trumpets to sound the battle cry against you. People of Israel, do not fight against the LORD, the God of your ancestors, for you will not succeed." ¹³ Meanwhile Jeroboam had sent a detachment around to ambush them from behind. His troops were in front of Judah, and the ambush was behind them. ¹⁴ When Judah looked around and saw that they were being attacked from front and rear, they cried out to the LORD. The priests blew their trumpets ¹⁵ and the men of Judah raised the battle cry. At the sound of their shout, God routed Jeroboam and all Israel before Abijah and Judah.

¹⁶ The Israelites fled before Judah, and God gave them into their hands. ¹⁷ Abijah and his troops inflicted devastating losses on them — five hundred thousand of Israel's finest soldiers fell slain. ¹⁸ The Israelites were subdued on that day, and the people of Judah prevailed because they relied on the LORD, the God of their ancestors. ¹⁹ Abijah pursued Jeroboam and captured cities from him — Bethel, Jeshanah, and Ephron, along with their surrounding villages. ²⁰ Jeroboam did not recover his power during the time of Abijah. And the LORD struck him down, and he died.

²¹ But Abijah grew stronger. He married fourteen wives and was the father of twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters. ²² The rest of the acts of Abijah, his ways, and his words are recorded in the writings of the prophet Iddo.
